query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A low‐temperature plasma nitriding treatment applied to TC4 (Ti6Al4V) will create a nitrogen‐enriched hardened surface layer, thereby significantly improving its hardness and wear resistance without degrading its bulk mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified α + β dual‐phase TC4 (Ti6Al4V) alloy with standard microstructure and baseline hardness/wear performance.
generation.intervention: Apply low-temperature plasma nitriding to the TC4 alloy surface using controlled temperature and time parameters that promote nitrogen diffusion without altering the substrate’s beneficial microstructure.
generation.conditions: Treatment performed at a temperature low enough (typically 500–600°C or lower for plasma nitriding of titanium alloys) to avoid extensive α-case formation, under a controlled nitrogen atmosphere; wear tests performed under high-contact-stress conditions at room or moderate elevated temperatures relevant to the intended application.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a thin, diffusion-hardened nitrogen-enriched surface layer (containing Ti–N phases such as TiN and/or solid-solution strengthened α-Ti) that transitions gradually to the unmodified bulk microstructure.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen incorporation into the surface leads to the formation of hard nitride phases and/or solid-solution strengthening of the α-phase. The resulting hardened layer increases resistance to plastic deformation and wear, while the gradient microstructure minimizes adverse effects on the substrate’s toughness and fatigue resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to untreated TC4, the plasma nitrided samples are expected to exhibit a marked increase in surface hardness and reduced wear rate. The beneficial core properties (e.g., ductility, high specific strength) will be largely maintained due to limited penetration depth of the nitriding process.
generation.baseline: The untreated TC4 alloy exhibits low hardness and poor friction and wear properties under extreme service, high-contact-stress conditions.
generation.boundary: The improvement is anticipated under conditions where surface-initiated damage is critical (e.g., sliding wear or contact fatigue tests) and for applications within the operational temperature range that does not promote further phase transformations or oxidation of the modified layer.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the optimal nitriding parameters (e.g., time, temperature, gas composition) necessary to maximize surface hardness and wear resistance without introducing brittleness or an overly thick hardened layer that could compromise fatigue properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of TC4 samples: one set subjected to the optimized low-temperature plasma nitriding treatment and a control set of untreated TC4. Conduct standardized microhardness tests (e.g., Vickers hardness), pin-on-disk wear tests, and fatigue or impact testing to evaluate changes in mechanical properties. Characterize the surface layer thickness and phase composition using SEM and XRD.
measurements: Surface hardness (Vickers hardness measurements) of the nitrided layer vs. untreated surface
Wear rate (mass loss or volume loss) under identical sliding wear conditions
Microstructural analysis (thickness and phase identification of the hardened layer)
Bulk mechanical tests (fatigue/impact) to ensure no detrimental effects on toughness
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nitrided samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in surface hardness and a corresponding reduction in wear rate compared to untreated TC4, or if they exhibit a significant drop in bulk mechanical properties (e.g., reduced fatigue toughness), then the hypothesis is falsified.
